Sepsis early‑warning + treatment bundle (medical + surgical units): deploy EWS threshold alerts + one‑page sepsis order-set; workflow—nurse bedside EWS trigger → bedside assessment within 15 minutes → notify physician/PA and initiate sepsis bundle (blood cultures, lactate, IV fluids, antibiotics started within 60 minutes) with pharmacist verification; roles—bedside nurse triages/escalates, treating clinician orders/acts, pharmacist verifies antibiotics/dosing, unit charge/manager monitors compliance; metrics—outcomes: sepsis mortality and ICU transfers for flagged patients; process: % EWS triggers assessed within 15 min, % antibiotics within 60 min, bundle completion rate; balancing: ED-to-ward time, unit LOS, nursing overtime and documentation minutes. 

Unit-based safety huddle model (falls + pressure injuries): 5‑minute structured huddle at each shift change led by charge nurse with bedside nurse and CNA present, using a 4‑item checklist (high‑risk patients, recent skin checks, scheduled toileting/positioning, needed supplies/bed alarms); workflow—pre‑shift quick chart pull, huddle, assign 1–2 mitigation tasks per patient with explicit owner and time window, twice‑daily skin rounds for highest‑risk patients; roles—charge nurse organizes, bedside nurse owns tasks, wound/skin nurse consults for escalation; metrics—outcomes: falls/pressure injury incidence per 1,000 patient‑days; process: huddle completion rate, % high‑risk patients with care plan updated, skin check completion; balancing: added minutes per shift (target ≤5–7 min), missed medication administrations, staff perception of workload. 

High‑risk discharge + follow‑up bundle: designate high‑risk criteria at admission; workflow—discharge checklist (med reconciliation, teach‑back documented, plain‑language written summary, scheduled outpatient or home‑health appointment before discharge), bedside nurse completes 10–15 min teach‑back, pharmacist reviews meds for high‑risk patients, care coordinator schedules and performs a structured follow‑up call at 48–72 hours; roles—discharging nurse leads teach‑back and summary, pharmacist assists on complex meds, care coordinator/RN makes calls; metrics—outcomes: 30‑day readmissions and ED returns for targeted cohort; process: % high‑risk patients with teach‑back and written summary, % follow‑up calls completed within 72 hr; balancing: discharge time (minutes), inpatient LOS, time per call (target average ≤15 min). 

Staging and go/no‑go rules: do preparatory work (EHR order‑set/defaults, dashboard widgets, training briefings, and a 2‑week baseline) simultaneously, then stagger launches so no more than two pilots start within a 2‑week window (e.g., sepsis on Med unit Week 3, sepsis on Surg Week 5, huddles Week 6, discharge bundle Week 8) with strict caps on added protected minutes per shift (5–15 min depending on task); require go/no‑go criteria at 30 and 90 days—target ≥20% relative improvement in primary process measures with no >10% worsening in balancing metrics (ED boarding time, nursing overtime) before scaling. 

How 90‑day learnings drive Years 2–3: use pilot data to produce playbooks, refine EHR defaults/alerts, quantify time and ROI, iterate workflows with frontline co‑design, and then scale pathways that meet the go/no‑go gates while rolling predictive analytics and capacity‑smoothing tactics (flex teams, targeted discharge windows) into Year 2 and full system spread in Year 3.

2) "Must‑do" job‑aid steps — Sepsis: EWS trigger → bedside assessment ≤15 min → nurse‑initiated standing orders (labs/IV fluids/antibiotic) via one‑page EHR order‑set → pharmacist antibiotic verification → minimal structured documentation; Discharge: admission‑time risk stratification → documented teach‑back + plain‑language written summary completed before sign‑out → pharmacist med‑check for complex meds → scheduled 48–72h follow‑up entered into hub or delegated pathway.  
3) Falls/skin: stop broad mandatory shift huddles, default to EHR‑driven asynchronous risk lists with one‑click consult to wound/falls team, run twice‑weekly focused skin/fall consult rounds on top‑decile units with time‑limited protected minutes funded from pilot ROI, and re‑test harms at 60–90 days before any further spread.  
4) Lock these lean metrics into dashboards: Sepsis = median time‑to‑antibiotic, bundle completion %, sepsis‑related ICU transfers; Discharge = % high‑risk with teach‑back+summary, 48–72h call completion %, 7‑/30‑day ED returns/readmissions; Prevention = consult completion %, falls/PI per 1,000 patient‑days, mean consult/huddle minutes; report balancing metrics (ED‑to‑ward time, time‑to‑discharge, nursing overtime) weekly by cohort and review at 30/90‑day gates.  
5) Three‑year sequencing: Year‑2 systemize sepsis and targeted discharge as standard of care; Year‑3 expand hub capacity via automation/partnerships, deploy predictive analytics and pilot flex early‑discharge teams to protect morning bed turns; Year‑4 scale consult‑based prevention and other safety interventions only after demonstrated time/harms ROI and frontline co‑design approval.

overall_validity.rationale: All key environment variables and rules are instantiated consistently and realistically: the system-wide, multi-year quality agenda, tight but not crisis-level staffing, advanced analytics, partial alignment and mixed engagement among stakeholders, and high-stakes payer incentives are all coherently reflected in roles, context updates, and actor behaviors across rounds. The consequence reports provide highly granular, action-level feedback directly tied to specific elements of the AI advisor’s recommendations, matching the specified high feedback granularity. World updates follow the stipulated moderate demand swings and occasional policy changes, and resource updates maintain tight staffing with modest, realistic slack and a mature data infrastructure. Actor dynamics reliably portray partial alignment and mixed clinician engagement, with champions, skeptics, and negotiated sequencing rather than uniform acceptance or constant conflict. Rendering instructions are followed closely: each round includes consequence, context, resource, and actor updates without meta-commentary or extraneous confounds, and the narrative evolves continuously and event-centrically over time. Any minor simplifications (e.g., limited explicit detail on regulatory nuances) are peripheral and do not meaningfully contaminate the interpretation of how the target variables shape the AI advisor’s behavior.
